'''Hind Al-Abadleh''' (1977 or 1978 – 9 January 2025)<ref name="C&EN_obituary">{{cite news |last=Cottle |first=Sara |date=3 February 2025 |title=Obituary: Hind Al-Abadleh |url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-Hind-Al-Abadleh/103/web/2025/02 |work=Chemical & Engineering News |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250313181201/cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-Hind-Al-Abadleh/103/web/2025/02 |archive-date=13 March 2025 |access-date=30 March 2025}}</ref> was a professor of chemistry at [[Wilfrid Laurier University]] in [[Waterloo, Ontario]], Canada. She studied the physical chemistry of environmental interfaces, aerosols, and climate change.

== Early life and education ==
Al-Abadleh grew up in the [[United Arab Emirates]], where she became interested in chemistry during high school.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.canadianarabinstitute.org/people/person-watch/hind-al-abadleh/|title=Canadian Arab Institute :: Hind Al-Abadleh|website=www.canadianarabinstitute.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-03|archive-date=2020-01-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107220323/http://www.canadianarabinstitute.org/people/person-watch/hind-al-abadleh/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was excited that science could be used to protect the environment.<ref name=":0" /> In high school, she developed an interest in chemical impacts on the environment and went on to graduate as one of the top 10 students in the country. She eventually studied chemistry at the [[United Arab Emirates University]], graduating in 1999.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wlu-science-chem-halabadleh.ca/about-dr-hind-al-abadleh.html|title=About Dr. Hind Al-Abadleh|website=Al-Abadleh's research lab|language=en|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref> She joined the [[University of Iowa]] in 1999 for her doctoral studies, earning her PhD in 2003.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded the [[University of Iowa]] Dissertation Prize in Mathematics, Physical Sciences, and Engineering.<ref name=":1" />

== Research ==
She moved to [[Northwestern University]] for a postdoctoral scholarship working with [[Franz Geiger (chemist)|Franz Geiger]]. Whilst she loved [[Iowa]], 9/11 made America a hostile climate for [[Women in Islam|Muslim women]] (and men).<ref name=":0" /> She was appointed to the Department of Chemistry at [[Wilfrid Laurier University]] as an assistant professor in 2005 and was eventually promoted to Full Professor.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded a Research Corporation Cottrell College Science Award to study the surface interactions of [[Organoarsenic chemistry|organoarsenical compounds]] with geosorbents spectroscopically.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rescorp.org/gdresources/publications/annual_rpt07.pdf|title=Research Corporation Cottrell College Science Award|last=|first=|date=|website=Research Corporation|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226072907/http://rescorp.org/gdresources/publications/annual_rpt07.pdf|archive-date=2022-12-26|access-date=2018-10-03|url-status=dead}}</ref> Al-Abadleh held an adjunct professor appointment at the University of Waterloo.  She also was a visiting professor at the University of Toronto and Trent University (as the Inaugural Ray March Visiting Professor). The 2008 [[Petro-Canada]] award allowed her to study [[organic arsenic]] in soil and water.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.exchangemagazine.com/morningpost/2008/week31/Thursday/073117.html|title=Exchange Morning Post|website=www.exchangemagazine.com|access-date=2018-10-03|archive-date=2018-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004021210/http://www.exchangemagazine.com/morningpost/2008/week31/Thursday/073117.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her research has been supported by the [[American Chemical Society]], [[Ontario]]'s Ministry of Research and Innovation, [[Imperial Oil]] and the [[Canadian Foundation for Climate and Atmospheric Sciences]].<ref name=":1"/> She is studying the aging of aerosols using [[computational chemistry]], mathematical modelling and spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cheminst.ca/tags/hind-al-abadleh|title=Hind Al-Abadleh {{!}} The Chemical Institute of Canada|website=www.cheminst.ca|language=en|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Al-Abadleh|first=Hind A.|date=2015|title=Review of the bulk and surface chemistry of iron in atmospherically relevant systems containing humic-like substances|journal=RSC Advances|language=en|volume=5|issue=57|pages=45785–45811|doi=10.1039/C5RA03132J|bibcode=2015RSCAd...545785A |issn=2046-2069|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Ecohydrology Research Group">{{Cite news|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/ecohydrology/events/seminar-al-abadleh|title=Ecohydrology Seminar Series: Dr. Hind Al-Abadleh {{!}} Ecohydrology Research Group|date=2013-10-25|work=Ecohydrology Research Group|access-date=2018-10-03|language=en}}</ref> She gave a talk at 2014 [[TED (conference)|TED]]<nowiki/>x [[Laurier University]], ''To Dream and To Act''.<ref>{{Citation|last=TEDx Talks|title=To dream and to act: Hind Al-Abadleh at TEDxLaurierUniversity|date=2014-02-03|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LhCGoSoTMig|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref> In 2015 she published a study showing that aqueous phase reactions of guaiacol and catechol with iron lead to the formation of secondary colored particles. This study highlighted additional pathways for particle growth in the atmosphere in addition to particle nucleation and growth from gas-phase precursors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cheminst.ca/magazine/news/sunlight-plays-key-role-airborne-aerosol-gases|title=Sunlight plays key role in airborne aerosol gases {{!}} The Chemical Institute of Canada|website=www.cheminst.ca|language=en|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref>

In 2018 she was named the Fulbright [[Canada Research Chair]] in Climate Change and worked at the [[University of California, Irvine]], for 2019.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wlu.ca/news/spotlights/2018/sept/hind-al-abadleh-fulbright-scholar.html|title=Laurier chemistry professor Hind Al-Abadleh named Fulbright Scholar {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University|website=www.wlu.ca|language=en|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref> This position allowed her to teach a course on environmental catalysis and conduct research on multiphase chemistry in atmospheric aerosols catalyzed by metals.<ref name=":3" /> She was also a board member of ''Nano Ontario.''<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://maxgala.com/portfolio/dr-hind-a-al-abadleh/|title=Dr. Hind A. Al-Abadleh|work=MAX|access-date=2018-10-03|language=en-CA|archive-date=2021-05-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526151647/http://maxgala.com/portfolio/dr-hind-a-al-abadleh/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At Laurier, Dr. Al-Abadleh was honored with the 2023 Hoffman-Little Award for teaching, leadership, and collaboration; the 2021 University Research Professor Award, a Faculty Mentoring Award in 2015 and multiple Wilfrid Laurier University Faculty Association Merit Awards.  She was a fellow of the UK’s [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], a long-time member of the American Chemical Society and the Chemical Institute of Canada.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Wilfrid Laurier University |date=January 16, 2025 |title=Laurier mourns the passing of Professor Hind Al-Abadleh |url=https://www.wlu.ca/news/spotlights/2025/jan/laurier-mourns-the-passing-of-hind-al-abadleh.html |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Laurier News Hub, Spotlights.}}</ref>

In August 2024, Dr. Al-Abadleh began serving as department chair for Earth, Environmental and Resource Sciences at the University of Texas.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Linked In |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/hind-al-abadleh-873b5715/?originalSubdomain=ca |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=LinkedIn}}</ref> She died in January, 2025.<ref name=":4" />
